title: Q-BAG™
heroAlt: Speculative AI-generated image of a possible future Q888 artist-edition Q-Bag travelling through a cosmic landscape
heroDeclaration: Bring back a suitable coffee container you already own. Refill it. Mark it. Return again.
heroSupport: Q-Bag is Experiment 001 in Creative Afterlife: a small test of whether personal authorship and accumulated history can help an existing object stay in use.

imageDisclosure.label: Possible Future Q888 Edition · AI-Generated
imageDisclosure.text: This is one possible artist vessel, not the object required to participate. The experiment begins with something suitable you already have. The image was made with generative AI under my direction and may later be replaced, mutated, painted over, or respectfully composted.

introLead: Bring a suitable container you already own, buy coffee by weight, let refill evidence and personal expression accumulate, then bring the same object back. Q-Bag is a behaviour before it is a product.
protocolLead: The refill action should remain almost boring. Personalisation makes the object singular; repetition gives that singular object a cultural life.

protocolSteps.detail: Start with a clean, food-safe coffee container accepted by the café. No Q888 purchase is required.
The café weighs the empty container, adds coffee beans, and charges for the coffee.
A café stamp, refill mark, or occasional artist edition records that the performance happened.
Add exterior stickers, drawings, repairs, and memories. The owner is a co-author, not only a customer.
The loop repeats. Wear, marks, places, and stories become part of the object.

ageingLead: Ordinary packaging loses value as it ages. Q-Bag asks whether the opposite can happen: each return gives wear, marks, and memory another reason to remain.

ageingStages.title: A new container
ageingStages.detail: Clean, useful, and still replaceable. The story has not started.

ageingStages.title: A recognisable habit
ageingStages.detail: The first refill marks and personal stickers appear. A favourite café and a visual identity begin to repeat.

ageingStages.title: A personal archive
ageingStages.detail: Chosen stickers, drawings, artists, dates, stains, and journeys make this container unlike any other.

ageingStages.title: An object with gravity
ageingStages.detail: Throwing it away would mean discarding accumulated evidence of a life.

pilot.eyebrow: First Field Test · Edinburgh or Elsewhere
pilot.title: One café. A few returning objects. Three months.
pilot.body: The first pilot should be small enough to understand and strange enough to notice. Participants begin with suitable containers they already own; Edinburgh is the home base, not the boundary.
scope: A small group of people and their returning objects
measures: How often does each one return?
How many new retail coffee packages are avoided?
What do participants say makes them return?
pilot.metric: The magic metric is not bags sold. It is repeat returns per participating container.

operationalLayer.title: What happens behind the café counter?
operationalLayer.intro: Q-Bag should fit the equipment and rhythm a café already has. The first pilot tests a behaviour, not a new technology stack.

cafeFacts.label: Café does
cafeFacts.body: Tare the container, fill it with coffee beans, charge the customer, and add an optional refill mark.

cafeFacts.label: Café needs
cafeFacts.body: Existing scales, coffee beans, a clear reusable-container policy, and minimal additional counter time.

cafeFacts.label: Café gets
cafeFacts.body: Return visits, repeat bean sales, less packaging, participation in a visible artwork, and measured pilot results.

operationalLayer.pricingNote: The café chooses its own refill pricing. A discount is welcome, not required.
operationalLayer.backerIntro: A pilot backer helps existing containers enter a clear refill test, supports the café, and produces evidence before anyone is asked to believe in global scale.
funds: Pilot setup, container-suitability guidance, tare labels, and café instructions
Optional personalisation materials, Q888 marks, and collaborative editions
Pilot documentation, measurement, and practical support
evidence: New retail coffee packages avoided and café-counter lessons
Participant feedback about attachment, personalisation, and return
Operational friction, photographs, stories, and a visual archive
operationalLayer.closingNote: No platform. No app. No speculative machine required at the counter—only a suitable existing object, an ordinary refill, and enough attention to learn what happens next.

prototypeRecord.label: Prototype Record / V0
prototypeRecord.title: It existed before it had a system.
prototypeRecord.body: Before Q-Bag became a formal refill protocol, I reused a resealable Artisan Roast retail coffee bag, personalised it with stickers and collage, and carried it during travel. It lasted for some time. The behaviour and attachment were already real; the measured pilot comes next.
prototypeRecord.boundary: FIELD NOTE: These photographs document a personal prototype. They do not establish food-safety approval, freshness performance, or café workflow; those questions belong to V1.

participantCards.title: Clothing and repair
participantCards.body: Visible mending, alterations, patches, and accumulated decisions can continue a garment beyond its first finished identity.

participantCards.title: Packaging and components
participantCards.body: Boxes, containers, frames, spare parts, and useful fragments can become material for another purpose instead of an automatic disposal decision.

participantCards.title: Obsolete objects
participantCards.body: Damaged or discontinued things can receive repairs, combinations, new functions, or cultural lives their original manufacturers never specified.

valueCircuit.title: Participation is free. Objects can still fund what comes next.
valueCircuit.intro: Creative Afterlife does not require Q888 merchandise. Its commercial layer is optional and transparent: carefully made vessels, stickers, artist editions, tools, and collaborations can support the open behaviour and fund future experiments.

stages.label: Use what exists
stages.body: The core Q-Bag behaviour begins with a suitable container already in the participant's possession.

stages.label: Choose an artist vessel
stages.body: A purpose-designed durable Q888 edition may be bought by people who want one, never by people who merely want to participate.

stages.label: Add cultural layers
stages.body: Optional stickers, café marks, artist editions, and collaborations can add meaning without becoming compulsory proof of membership.

stages.label: Fund what comes next
stages.body: Revenue and evidence can support café pilots, artists, long-life objects, travel, and future Q888 work.

valueCircuit.collectorBonus: An open practice can still produce things worth buying. Creative meaning and financial survival are not enemies; each can help the other remain alive.
valueCircuit.clarityNote: NO Q888 PURCHASE IS REQUIRED. OPTIONAL EDITIONS MAY BE SOLD. COLLECTABILITY MAY EMERGE, BUT IT IS NEVER PROMISED.

speculativeBoundary.title: A proposed name for what may already be beginning.
speculativeBoundary.body: If Creative Afterlife travels across many kinds of objects, a larger cultural layer may become visible: ordinary manufactured things repaired, combined, painted, modified, and continued by their owners.
speculativeBoundary.classification: Historical period? Aesthetic movement? Coping mechanism? Or something we help manufacture by naming it too early. Classification remains unstable.

artworkCardDescription: The earlier collage organism: Infocigan fragments, stickers, speculative bag designs, and cultural artefacts from Q-Bag's product-first phase.

conceptCards.title: Don't replace the object. Continue its biography.
paragraphs: Creative Afterlife treats existing objects as unfinished rather than expired. People can repair, decorate, combine, paint, modify, collage, add history, and continue an object's biography instead of accepting its first commercial identity as final.
Q-Bag is Experiment 001. Coffee keeps the first test small, repetitive, and measurable: can creative attachment help a suitable container return again and again?

conceptCards.title: A quiet future assistant
paragraphs: AI could eventually help people imagine transformations using materials already around them, then return the work to human hands.

conceptCards.title: Q888 editions are optional
paragraphs: A purpose-designed durable Q-Bag, a Q888 sticker, or an artist edition may become a desirable commercial layer for people who want one.
Nobody needs to buy Q888 merchandise to join the refill behaviour. The paid objects help fund the open experiment; they do not certify who belongs.

conceptCards.title: The Adaptation Layer
paragraphs: Across decades, millions of uncoordinated acts of repair, alteration, decoration, and reuse might form a recognisable historical record of how humans adapted to material abundance and mass production.
Future historians might recognise it as the moment mass production stopped being the final author of an object.

partnersParagraphs: Q-Bag is designed to meet coffee businesses where refill behaviour already exists: a tare-and-fill routine, a clear reusable-container policy, light-touch marks, and occasional collaborative editions. Revenue and experience from optional objects can be reinvested into pilots, artists, travel, and future Q888 projects.

The immediate invitation is not to scale a bag company. It is to find the right first café—in Edinburgh or anywhere in the world—willing to host and measure a small existing-container experiment. Edinburgh is where I am; the protocol is willing to travel.
closingLines: Add a life it did not arrive with.
Let history decide what layer appeared.
